quetions.title: Reveal Cards in Increasing Order
quetions.content:
You are given an integer array deck representing a deck of unique cards.

You must arrange the deck so that when you repeatedly reveal the top card and move the next card to the bottom, the revealed cards appear in increasing order.

Return the ordering of the deck that achieves this.

solutions.code:
from collections import deque

def deckRevealedIncreasing(deck):
    deck.sort()
    q=deque(range(len(deck)))
    res=[0]*len(deck)

    for card in deck:
        i=q.popleft()
        res[i]=card
        if q:
            q.append(q.popleft())

    return res

quetions.title: Winner of the Circular Game
quetions.content:
There are n friends standing in a circle. Starting from the first friend, count k people clockwise including the current one. The kth friend leaves the circle.

The process continues until only one person remains.

Return the winner.

solutions.code:
from collections import deque

def findTheWinner(n,k):
    q=deque(range(1,n+1))

    while len(q)>1:
        q.rotate(-(k-1))
        q.popleft()

    return q[0]

quetions.title: Maximum Robots Within Budget
quetions.content:
You are given arrays chargeTimes and runningCosts and an integer budget.

The cost of running k robots is:
max(chargeTimes) + k * sum(runningCosts)

Find the maximum number of robots that can run simultaneously without exceeding the budget.
quetions.inputFormat: Arrays chargeTimes, runningCosts, and integer budget.

solutions.code:
from collections import deque

def maximumRobots(chargeTimes,runningCosts,budget):
    q=deque()
    total=0
    left=0
    ans=0

    for right in range(len(chargeTimes)):
        while q and chargeTimes[q[-1]]<=chargeTimes[right]:
            q.pop()
        q.append(right)

        total+=runningCosts[right]

        while q and chargeTimes[q[0]]+(right-left+1)*total>budget:
            if q[0]==left: q.popleft()
            total-=runningCosts[left]
            left+=1

        ans=max(ans,right-left+1)

    return ans

quetions.title: Time Taken to Cross the Door
quetions.content:
There is a door that people can use to either enter or exit a room. Each person arrives at a given time and wants to either enter (0) or exit (1).

Only one person can cross the door per second.

If both sides are waiting, the door gives priority to the person who used the door in the previous second.

Return an array where the ith value is the time when the ith person crosses the door.

solutions.code:
from collections import deque

def timeTaken(arrival,state):
    n=len(arrival)
    enter=deque()
    exit=deque()
    res=[0]*n

    time=0
    i=0
    last=-1

    while i<n or enter or exit:
        while i<n and arrival[i]<=time:
            (exit if state[i]==1 else enter).append(i)
            i+=1

        if exit or enter:
            if exit and (last==1 or not enter):
                idx=exit.popleft()
                last=1
            else:
                idx=enter.popleft()
                last=0

            res[idx]=time
            time+=1
        else:
            time=arrival[i]
            last=-1

    return res

quetions.title: Design Circular Deque
quetions.content:
Design a circular double-ended queue (deque).

Implement the MyCircularDeque class:
- insertFront()
- insertLast()
- deleteFront()
- deleteLast()
- getFront()
- getRear()
- isEmpty()
- isFull()
quetions.inputFormat: Deque capacity k followed by operations.
quetions.outputFormat: Return boolean or values depending on operation.

solutions.code:
class MyCircularDeque:
    def __init__(self,k):
        self.q=[0]*k
        self.head=0
        self.count=0
        self.size=k

    def insertFront(self,val):
        if self.count==self.size: return False
        self.head=(self.head-1)%self.size
        self.q[self.head]=val
        self.count+=1
        return True

    def insertLast(self,val):
        if self.count==self.size: return False
        tail=(self.head+self.count)%self.size
        self.q[tail]=val
        self.count+=1
        return True

    def deleteFront(self):
        if self.count==0: return False
        self.head=(self.head+1)%self.size
        self.count-=1
        return True

    def deleteLast(self):
        if self.count==0: return False
        self.count-=1
        return True

    def getFront(self): return -1 if self.count==0 else self.q[self.head]

    def getRear(self): return -1 if self.count==0 else self.q[(self.head+self.count-1)%self.size]

    def isEmpty(self): return self.count==0

    def isFull(self): return self.count==self.size

quetions.title: Maximum Average Subarray of Fixed Window
quetions.content: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the maximum average value of any contiguous subarray of length k.

solutions.code:
def findMaxAverage(nums,k):
    window=sum(nums[:k])
    max_sum=window

    for i in range(k,len(nums)):
        window+=nums[i]-nums[i-k]
        max_sum=max(max_sum,window)

    return max_sum/k

quetions.title: Sum of Subarray Minimum Values
quetions.content:
Given an array of integers arr, return the sum of the minimum value of every subarray.

Since the answer may be large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7.
quetions.outputFormat: Return sum of minimum values of all subarrays.

solutions.code:
def sumSubarrayMins(arr):
    MOD=10**9+7
    stack=[]
    res=0

    for i in range(len(arr)+1):
        cur=arr[i] if i<len(arr) else 0

        while stack and arr[stack[-1]]>cur:
            mid=stack.pop()
            left=stack[-1] if stack else -1
            right=i
            res+=arr[mid]*(mid-left)*(right-mid)

        stack.append(i)

    return res%MOD

quetions.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
quetions.content: Given an array heights representing the histogram's bar height where the width of each bar is 1, return the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed within the histogram.

solutions.code:
def largestRectangleArea(heights):
    stack=[]
    res=0

    for i in range(len(heights)+1):
        cur=heights[i] if i<len(heights) else 0

        while stack and heights[stack[-1]]>cur:
            h=heights[stack.pop()]
            w=i if not stack else i-stack[-1]-1
            res=max(res,h*w)

        stack.append(i)

    return res
